questions.q:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

The government should take stringent steps against terrorists and foil their ______ designs.
questions.s:
The correct answer is: Option 2.

Key Points

  • The word "malicious" means having or showing a desire to cause harm to someone; intending to do harm. (दुर्भावनापूर्ण)
    • Example: The hacker was arrested for his malicious activities online.
  • The word "stringent" refers to something that is strict, precise, and exacting. (कठोर)
    • Example: The new regulations are very stringent and leave no room for error.
  • Hence, we can infer that the correct word to describe the terrorists' designs would be "malicious".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Exemplary (उदाहरणीय): Serving as a desirable model; representing the best of its kind.
    • Example: His exemplary behavior earned him the respect of his peers.
  • Conducive (अनुकूल): Making a certain situation or outcome likely or possible.
    • Example: The quiet environment is conducive to studying.
  • Benevolent (परमार्थी): Well-meaning and kindly.
    • Example: The benevolent gentleman donated a large sum to the orphanage.

questions.q:
In the question given below, three sentences are given which may or may not contain an error. Choose the one that is grammatically incorrect.

I. This watch is more expensive of the five watches he has been gifted.

II. Raghav, in my opinion, is humbler than loyal.

III. This watch is the more expensive of the two watches.
questions.s:
Sentences I and II are incorrect.

I: A comparative degree is used to compare two things. In the given sentence, the superlative degree should be used to talk about one of the five watches.

The correct sentence is: This watch is the most expensive of the five watches he has been gifted.

II: When two qualities in the same person or thing are compared, the comparative

degree is formed by using more, instead of - r or - er with the positive. So, 'humbler' should be replaced with 'more humble'.

The correct sentence is: Raghav, in my opinion, is more humble than loyal.

III: When the selection of one of the two persons or things (sets of things) of the same kind is meant, the comparative degree is preceded by 'the' and is followed by 'of'. So, sentence III is correct.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.
